gaps.title: Rejection logging and audit entry content undefined
gaps.description: REQ-002 requires every approval and rejection to be recorded, but the only audit row shown in the capture is an approval ('Approved EXP-71'); a rejection entry is not shown in the capture. The audit table shows only When, Who and Action; whether an entry must also record the claim amount, claimant, decision reason or the approver's role is not defined, and CQ-003 (entry content) has no recorded answer.
gaps.why_it_matters: REQ-002 is a must-have and the audit log is what finance staff export (REQ-003); if rejections or key fields are not captured, the log cannot show who decided what on which claim.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The audit log may omit rejections or lack the fields needed to reconstruct a decision, failing the must-have requirement and making the exported CSV incomplete.
research_questions: Which fields do established audit-trail guidelines (for example OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet, NIST SP 800-92) recommend recording for an approval or rejection event?
What do expense-management products typically record in an approval audit entry (claim reference, amount, approver, decision, reason, timestamp)?

gaps.title: Who may view the audit log and who may export it
gaps.description: REQ-003 says finance staff can export the audit log, but whether export is limited to finance staff, and who may view the audit log at all (managers, finance, employees about their own claims), is not defined. The capture shows an enabled Export CSV button and an Audit log link on the approvals screen with no role indication.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-005 'Who may export the audit log?'
ambiguous_behaviours SCR-004 'Who can view the audit log?'

gaps.why_it_matters: The audit log lists employee names, claims and approver identities; the Audit log link sits on a manager-facing screen, so it is unclear whether managers see decisions made by other managers or can export them.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Access to the audit log and its export cannot be specified, risking exposure of other teams' expense data or blocking finance staff who need it.

gaps.title: Approver coverage when the direct-report rule does not fit
gaps.description: DEC-001 limits approval to the claimant's own manager. What happens to claims from employees with no manager, from top-level managers, while a manager is absent, or when a reporting line changes while a claim is pending is not defined. Whether managers see claims from employees who are not their direct reports on the approvals screen is not shown in the capture.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-003 'Who may approve or reject a claim'

gaps.why_it_matters: The direct-report rule leaves some claims without an eligible approver and makes pending claims depend on organisation data that can change.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Some claims could never be approved, or could be approved by a former manager after a reporting change.

gaps.title: Rejection reason not defined
gaps.description: Whether a manager must, may or cannot give a reason when rejecting a claim is not defined (CQ-002 has no recorded answer). The capture shows a Reject button with no reason field; a reject dialog or form is not shown in the capture.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-003 'Is a reason or comment required or possible on Reject?'

gaps.why_it_matters: A rejection reason affects what the claimant learns, what the audit log records (REQ-002) and what finance staff see in the export.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The Reject interaction and the rejection audit entry cannot be specified.

gaps.title: Audit log retention and protection from change
gaps.description: How long audit entries must be kept, whether they may ever be edited or deleted, and by whom, is not defined (CQ-003 has no recorded answer).

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-004 'How long are entries kept'

gaps.why_it_matters: The audit log records financial approvals; its value as evidence depends on entries being kept long enough and not being altered.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The log may be purged too early or be alterable, undermining REQ-002 and any financial record-keeping obligations.
research_questions: What retention periods apply to expense and approval records under UK record-keeping rules (for example HMRC guidance on business records), given amounts are shown in GBP?
What established practices make an application audit log tamper-evident or append-only?

gaps.title: Outcome, confirmation and undo after Approve or Reject
gaps.description: What the approvals screen shows after Approve or Reject (row removed, status shown, success message), whether either action asks for confirmation, and whether a decision can be undone or changed are not shown in the capture and not defined. No success, error or confirmation state was captured.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-003 'What happens to the row after Approve or Reject'
ambiguous_behaviours SCR-003 'Can an approval or rejection be undone or changed?'

gaps.why_it_matters: Approve and Reject sit side by side on each row with no observed confirmation; a mis-click decides a claim, and any reversal must itself be audited under REQ-002.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Accidental decisions may be irreversible, or reversals may happen without being recorded.
research_questions: What patterns do established design systems (for example GOV.UK Design System, Material) recommend for confirming or undoing consequential approve/reject actions in a table row?

gaps.title: Failure, double submission and retry of decisions
gaps.description: What happens when Approve or Reject fails, is clicked twice, or is retried after a lost connection is not defined, including whether this can create a missing or duplicate audit entry. No error or loading state was captured.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-003 'What happens on failure, or if another approver acts on the same claim at the same time?'

gaps.why_it_matters: REQ-002 says every decision must be recorded; a decision that is applied but not logged, or logged twice, breaks the audit trail finance staff export.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The audit log could disagree with claim outcomes, or a claim could receive conflicting decisions.
research_questions: What established techniques (for example idempotency keys, transactional outbox) keep a state change and its audit record consistent under retries and failures?

gaps.title: Export scope, columns and limits
gaps.description: DEC-002 settles the format as CSV of audit log entries, but whether the export covers all entries or can be filtered (date range, manager, claim), which columns it contains, how large exports behave, and whether the export itself is recorded are not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: The audit log grows with every decision; finance staff exporting it need a predictable scope, and the export moves employee expense data out of the product.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The export may be too large to use, miss the period finance needs, or leave no record of who extracted the data.

gaps.title: Untrusted text in exported CSV
gaps.description: The audit log and claims contain free text entered by employees (for example the claim description 'Train to Leeds'); the CSV export will carry this text into spreadsheet software. How such content is handled in the export is not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: Finance staff will open the CSV in spreadsheet tools, so text an employee typed into a claim could be interpreted as a formula on a finance user's machine.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Exported files could execute attacker-controlled formulas or corrupt finance staff's data.
research_questions: What does the OWASP guidance on CSV injection recommend for exporting user-supplied text to CSV?
Which CSV conventions (RFC 4180, encoding, currency and date formatting) do common spreadsheet tools such as Excel and Google Sheets handle reliably?

gaps.title: Accessible names for row actions and table
gaps.description: The claims table has an unlabeled actions column, and each row's buttons are labelled only 'Approve' and 'Reject' with no visible link to the claim. How screen-reader and keyboard users identify which claim a button acts on, and how the outcome is announced, is not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: With many claims, identical 'Approve' buttons are indistinguishable out of context, so assistive-technology users could approve the wrong claim.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The approvals screen may fail WCAG 2.2 AA and lead to wrong decisions by assistive-technology users.
research_questions: Which WCAG 2.2 success criteria (for example 1.3.1, 2.4.6, 4.1.2, 4.1.3) apply to repeated action buttons in data table rows and to announcing the result of an action?
What pattern does the GOV.UK Design System or WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices give for table row actions with unique accessible names?

gaps.title: Empty, loading and high-volume list behaviour
gaps.description: Both screens were captured with a single row. How the claims list and the audit log appear with no data, while loading, or with many records (ordering, paging, sorting, filtering) is not shown in the capture and not defined.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-003 'How are claims listed when there are none or many'
ambiguous_behaviours SCR-004 'how are they ordered, filtered or paged' / 'How is an empty audit log shown?'

gaps.why_it_matters: The audit log is append-only by nature of REQ-002 and will keep growing; managers with many direct reports may have many pending claims.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Screens may become unusable at volume, and empty states may be mistaken for errors.

gaps.title: Navigation back from the audit log and entry point for finance
gaps.description: No navigation back from the Audit log screen is visible in the capture. The only observed entry to the audit log is a link on the manager-facing approvals screen; how finance staff, who export the log, reach it is not shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: Finance staff are the named users of the export (REQ-003) but the only observed route runs through the approvals screen.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The export workflow for finance staff has no defined entry or exit.

gaps.title: Notifications and what follows a decision
gaps.description: Whether the claimant (or finance) is told when a claim is approved or rejected, through which channel, and what follows (payment, resubmission of a rejected claim) is not defined.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-003 'what notifications or downstream payment follow?'

gaps.why_it_matters: Employees are reimbursed only after approval; without a defined follow-up, claimants may not learn the outcome or how to correct a rejected claim.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The end of the approval workflow stays unspecified.

gaps.title: Audit timestamp precision and time zone
gaps.description: The audit row shows '2 Mar 10:14' with no year or time zone. How timestamps are stored, shown and written to the CSV export is not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: Audit entries retained across years and exported for finance need unambiguous dates and times to order and reconcile decisions.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Exported entries may be ambiguous across years, time zones or daylight-saving changes.
research_questions: What timestamp format (for example ISO 8601 with UTC offset) is recommended for audit records and CSV exports intended for spreadsheet use?

assumptions.text: DEC-001 ('own direct reports only') is taken to exclude a manager approving their own claim, so self-approval is not raised as a separate gap.
assumptions.why: CQ-002 asked about self-approval and has no explicit answer, but a manager is not their own direct report.
assumptions.impact: If self-approval is somehow possible (for example a manager listed as their own report), a control gap reappears.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm with the customer that managers can never approve or reject their own claims.

assumptions.text: DEC-002 is taken to settle the export format (CSV of audit log entries) but not its filtering, columns or size limits.
assumptions.why: The answer to CQ-004 addresses format only; filtering was part of the question but not answered.
assumptions.impact: Export scope remains open as GAP-008.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm whether 'the audit log entries' means always the full log.

proposed_status_changes.reason: Audit entry content, rejection logging, retention and protection from change are not defined; CQ-003 has no recorded answer (see GAP-001, GAP-005).
